title: IceNet: seasonal forecasts of Arctic sea ice
summary: The model outperforms ECMWF’s SEAS5 dynamical system in seasonal forecasts of summer sea ice, especially for extreme events, and is over 2,000 times faster (under ten seconds on a GPU). SEAS5 is better at a one-month lead, and the September comparison covers nine years; published in Nature Communications.
organization: British Antarctic Survey, Alan Turing Institute, and others

evidence.tested: IceNet is compared with the SEAS5 dynamical model in seasonal summer sea-ice forecasts, especially extreme events.
evidence.unknown: Not reported in the abstract read.
evidence.ai_role: Probabilistic deep-learning model forecast the next six months of sea-ice concentration.
